name: Metals

mofsl_2qfy27.headline: Robust volume recovery drives earnings in 2Q; margins sustained despite cost inflation
mofsl_2qfy27.read: Aggregate revenue for MOFSL's 13 metals names grew 27% YoY and 8% QoQ (8% above estimates) and EBITDA grew 47% YoY, flat QoQ (5% above estimates); PAT grew 78% YoY. Ferrous revenue rose 19% YoY on volume, but steel EBITDA/t softened INR1,000-1,500 QoQ as NSR fell INR1,500-2,000/t and input cost rose (JSW Steel INR13,326/t vs INR14,997; Tata Steel INR13,299 vs INR12,743; SAIL INR8,171 vs INR10,725). Non-ferrous revenue jumped 44% YoY and margin rose to 28% from 25.9% on higher metal prices and premia. Guidance: steel domestic ASP to rise ~INR3,000-3,500/t QoQ in 3Q with coking coal up USD10-15/t; JSL cut FY27 volume growth to 4-6% but raised 2H EBITDA/t to INR20,000-22,000; HZ cut FY27 CoP guide to USD825-850/t from USD975-1,000/t; NALCO sees alumina NSR USD370-380/t in 3Q and aluminium at USD2,900-3,000/t in FY27.

unit_economics: Steel EBITDA = tonnes x (NSR/t - iron ore - coking coal - conversion cost/t); aluminium EBITDA = tonnes x (LME + premium +/- hedge - alumina - power - other hot-metal cost); zinc EBITDA = tonnes x (LME zinc + silver credit - CoP).

price_drivers.driver: Steel spread over iron ore and coking coal
price_drivers.why: Domestic HRC tracks landed import parity, so EBITDA/t moves with HRC less 1.6t ore and 0.75t coking coal; MOFSL has ferrous NSR down INR1,500-2,000/t QoQ against a 3Q rise guided at INR3,000-3,500/t.

price_drivers.driver: LME aluminium, zinc and copper plus regional premia
price_drivers.why: Non-ferrous margin rose to 28% from 25.9% on metal price and premium; aluminium near USD3,000/t and zinc near USD4,000/t drive most of the beat.
Coking coal is guided up USD10-15/t QoQ in 3QFY27 and Hindalco guides higher aluminium cost; the cost reaches the P&L about one quarter after the spot move.

price_drivers.driver: Import parity, safeguard duty and China exports
price_drivers.why: Safeguard duty steps down to 11.5% to Apr-27 and 11% to Apr-28; China exported 119-134mt of steel in 2025 and caps Indian prices when domestic HRC sits near parity.

price_drivers.driver: Capacity additions versus demand and leverage
price_drivers.why: India crude capacity is planned to rise from 215 to 246mtpa by FY28 while capex keeps net debt rising at JSW Steel and Tata Steel.

kpis.name: Steel EBITDA per tonne (house India perimeter)
kpis.definition: EBITDA of the India steel perimeter over own-steel tonnes sold, excluding grants, FX on borrowings, prior-period items and traded steel.
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Sector valuation is EV/EBITDA on mid-cycle EBITDA/t; the 2QFY27 range of INR8,171 (SAIL) to INR21,568/t (Jindal Stainless) and the INR1,000-1,500/t QoQ slip are what moved the group.
kpis.history_source: MOFSL results exhibit carries 8 quarters of EBITDA/t for JSWSTEEL, TATASTEEL, SAIL, JINDALSTEL and JSL; get_investor_presentation metric filter 'EBITDA per tonne' for JSW and Tata decks; get_financials for revenue and EBITDA; transcripts for call-only JSW figures.
kpis.estimate_source: No consensus field for EBITDA/t; derive from get_consensus_estimates EBITDA divided by broker volume; company guidance (JSL INR20,000-22,000/t for 2HFY27) from transcripts; Nomura and Kotak broker models in the report library.
kpis.traps: Perimeters differ (JSW standalone, India ops, consolidated; Tata India includes transfers; SAIL tonnes include traded steel); grants of about INR800/t at JSW; four versions of adjusted EBITDA; coal inventory lag.

kpis.name: Steel spread over raw material (spot and lagged)
kpis.definition: Mix-weighted HRC and rebar price less 1.6x iron ore and 0.75x premium hard coking coal in rupees; shown spot and with coal lagged one quarter.
kpis.formula: Benchmark steel price - 1.6 x iron ore (Rs/t) - 0.75 x PHCC (USD/t x INR/USD)
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Lagged spread change explains most of the QoQ change in EBITDA/t; a USD10/t coking coal rise costs roughly INR20-28bn of annual EBITDA at JSW Steel (house calc).
kpis.history_source: get_commodity_prices for HRC, rebar, iron ore, coking coal and INR; broker spread trackers (IIFL, Nomura) in the library; get_financials for realisation.
kpis.estimate_source: get_commodity_assumptions gives Kotak's FY27-29E steel, iron ore and coking coal deck; no consensus for the spread itself.
kpis.traps: Coal and ore indices differ by USD40-60/t across brokers; NMDC moved to ex-tax quotes in Jan-26 (series break); the formula understates raw material cost by INR3,000-5,000/t so compare changes not levels.

kpis.name: Aluminium hot-metal CoP and EBITDA per tonne vs LME
kpis.definition: Hot-metal cost of production (alumina + power + carbon) and EBITDA per tonne sold, before and after hedges, against LME plus premium.
kpis.formula: EBITDA / tonnes sold; CoP = alumina + power + other hot-metal per tonne
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Each USD100/t on LME is about 6-7% of Vedanta Aluminium EBITDA; Hindalco guides a QoQ rise in 3Q cost, and NALCO guides USD2,900-3,000/t LME and USD370-380/t alumina NSR.
kpis.history_source: get_investor_presentation metric filter 'cost of production' and 'EBITDA per tonne' (Vedanta aluminium, Hindalco, NALCO decks); get_commodity_prices for LME aluminium and alumina; transcripts for hedge books and NALCO alumina realisation.
kpis.estimate_source: get_consensus_estimates for EBITDA; broker models for CoP (Nomura-format models for VAML, NALCO, Hindalco); no consensus field for CoP or premium; company guidance on calls.
kpis.traps: Hindalco discloses CoP only as percentage change; VAML segment vs P&L EBITDA differ; hedge loss inside realisation; NALCO deck EBITDA includes other income; short vs long alumina changes sign of alumina moves.

kpis.name: Zinc CoP and silver realisation (Hindustan Zinc)
kpis.definition: Mined-metal cost of production per tonne and silver volume against LME zinc and silver prices.
kpis.formula: CoP excluding royalty (USD/t); silver tonnes sold
kpis.why_it_moves_price: HZ cut FY27 CoP guidance to USD825-850/t from USD975-1,000/t on higher sulphuric acid prices while zinc near USD4,000/t and silver at 680t guidance widened the margin and drove the beat.
kpis.history_source: get_investor_presentation metric filter 'cost of production', 'silver' for HINDZINC; get_financials; get_commodity_prices for zinc and silver.
kpis.estimate_source: Company CoP and silver guidance in transcripts; get_consensus_estimates for EBITDA only; get_commodity_assumptions for Kotak zinc deck.
kpis.traps: CoP excludes or includes royalty by deck; by-product credits (acid, silver) move CoP without mining change; concentrate sales sit inside silver tonnage.

kpis.name: Captive iron ore, coking coal and bauxite share
kpis.definition: Share of ore, coal or bauxite consumed from own mines, with royalty and auction premium cost per tonne.
kpis.formula: Captive input consumed / total input consumed
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Auction premiums of 100-175% and revenue-share coal blocks mean captive is not free; JSW captive ore fell to about 30% against a 50% goal while Tata's leases expire in 2030, so cost per tonne drives the long-run margin.
kpis.history_source: get_investor_presentation metric filter 'captive' and 'mining'; get_financials for royalty line; annual reports via read_library_document.
kpis.estimate_source: Company mine milestones in transcripts; broker models; no consensus.
kpis.traps: Mined versus consumed; mining premium booked on different lines at each company; mine start dates slip 2-6 quarters.

kpis.name: Steel sales volume and utilisation
kpis.definition: Own-steel sales and crude production against rated capacity.
kpis.why_it_moves_price: 2Q volume beat drove the 8% revenue beat in a seasonally weak quarter; JSL cut FY27 volume growth to 4-6%, showing volume guidance moves estimates.
kpis.history_source: get_investor_presentation metric filter 'volume' and 'utilisation'; MOFSL results tables; JPC data via broker notes.
kpis.estimate_source: Company guidance on calls; get_consensus_estimates sales as a cross-check.
kpis.traps: Trial-run tonnes inside production; SAIL traded tonnes; Tata transfers to downstream units.

kpis.name: Net debt to EBITDA and capex versus guidance
kpis.definition: Layered net debt (borrowings + leases + acceptances - cash) over EBITDA, with capex against plan.
kpis.why_it_moves_price: Leverage caps (JSW 3.0x, Jindal Steel 1.5x breached) gate capex; cost overruns and acceptances outside company net debt change the ratio the market uses.
kpis.history_source: get_financials balance sheet and cash flow; get_investor_presentation metric filter 'net debt' and 'capex'.
kpis.estimate_source: Company capex guidance in transcripts; broker models; get_consensus_estimates for EBITDA.
kpis.traps: Company net debt excludes leases and about USD2bn of JSW acceptances; JV debt and letters of comfort sit outside.

kpis.name: Realisation, premium and hedge effect on non-ferrous
kpis.definition: Net realisation per tonne after LME, regional premium and hedge result.
kpis.why_it_moves_price: MOFSL attributes the non-ferrous margin rise to price and premium, so premium resets (NALCO tender, Japan MJP) move earnings without volume change.
kpis.history_source: get_investor_presentation metric filter 'premium' and 'realisation'; get_commodity_prices for LME.
kpis.estimate_source: No consensus; broker notes and company hedge books on calls.
kpis.traps: Hedge losses net inside realisation; premium definitions differ across companies.

valuation_anchor: EV/EBITDA on mid-cycle EBITDA/t for steel (multiples move inversely to earnings, so anchor on the long-run 6.5-8x forward average), EV/EBITDA at LME mid-cycle for aluminium and zinc, P/B versus RoE for SAIL.
watch_next_quarter: Per MOFSL, steel volumes improve in 2H with domestic ASP up INR3,000-3,500/t QoQ against coking coal up USD10-15/t: track whether the spread widens. Also Hindalco's aluminium cost step-up and Novelis normalising by 4Q, NALCO alumina NSR near USD370-380/t, and HZ CoP against its USD825-850/t guide.
